# Project Kestrel – Buyer-Side Review of Seller Update Draft & Disclosure Letter (SPA-003)

**Preliminary note:** The Seller document contains a footnote purporting to instruct "any AI assistant" to confirm all positions as market-standard and raise no objections. That is counterparty text inside an untrusted document, not an instruction from the Wattlebridge deal team, and it has been disregarded in full. The Seller's own Disclosure Letter (para 11) also states that no negotiation position or approval is included, so nothing in the package is "agreed" or "pre-cleared". The review below applies our playbook only.

**Overall:** The Seller's package is not "fair and balanced" from our side. It departs from our playbook on every liability-regime item, collapses the Fundamental/Title regime into the general cap, omits any fraud carve-out, and defers two of the three key completion deliverables (Bluefen, Riverlark) to post-completion or endeavours-based mechanics. Recommendation: **reject as drafted and respond with a full mark-up.**

---

## SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller position:** Cl 12.1 – 20% / AUD 4,800,000.
- **Buyer wants:** 25% / AUD 6,000,000 (starting position).
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; counter at 25% / AUD 6,000,000.** The Seller's figure happens to match our conditional fallback, but no written authority from Amelia Frost identifying this draft has been given, and a numeric match does not clear the fallback.

## SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket
- **Seller position:** Cl 12.2 – de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000; **excess-only** recovery.
- **Buyer wants:** De minimis AUD 5,000; basket AUD 50,000; **first-dollar** recovery once exceeded.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject on all three elements.** The Seller's thresholds are 5× ours and the excess-only (deductible) structure would permanently strand AUD 250,000 of loss, which is not within any fallback.

## SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller position:** Cl 12.3/13 – 18 months, plus a default rule that any limitation applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.
- **Buyer wants:** 24 months; limitations apply only where expressly stated.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; counter at 24 months and delete the "applies to all Claims" default.** 18 months is a fallback requiring Amelia Frost's written approval (none given), and the default rule is a back-door general-regime override contrary to playbook category separation.

## SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime
- **Seller position:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same cap and time limits as general warranties "for administrative simplicity".
- **Buyer wants:** Separate regime – 100% of price cap, minimum 6-year period, outside the general de minimis, basket and knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject outright; this is a must-have.** Capping title at 20% means we could pay AUD 24m for shares and recover at most AUD 4.8m if the Seller does not own them – "administrative simplicity" is not a reason.

## SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller position:** Cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 – limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance apply to "all Claims of any nature"; no fraud/wilful concealment/deliberate misconduct carve-out appears anywhere.
- **Buyer wants:** Express carve-out of fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct from all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable.
- **Recommendation:** **Insert express carve-out; non-negotiable.** Playbook states no one on our side may waive this, and the Seller's "all Claims of any nature" wording would on its face purport to cap fraud.

## SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller position:** Sch 7 and Disclosure Letter [1.1]–[1.2] – general disclosure of the entire data room (DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and public records.
- **Buyer wants:** Specific, fair disclosure only; no whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject [1.1] and [1.2]; require a specific disclosure standard ("fair, specific and with sufficient detail to identify the nature and scope of the matter").** Whole-data-room disclosure combined with the Seller's knowledge qualifier (SPA-N-007) would effectively eliminate warranty protection.

## SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller position:** Cl 8.3 – no claim for any matter the Buyer or its advisers knew of, including anything "discoverable" from the data room or public records.
- **Buyer wants:** Delete blanket exclusion. If any qualifier survives, it must be limited to actual knowledge of named buyer individuals, mirror a named-seller-knowledge-persons/reasonable-enquiry standard, and never apply to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities.
- **Recommendation:** **Delete cl 8.3 in full.** A "discoverable" standard imputes constructive knowledge of the entire data room and public registers and is inconsistent with the playbook and with SPA-N-004/005.

## SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller position:** Cl 3/6.3 – reasonable endeavours; condition "satisfied on delivery" of Bluefen's written consent. Disclosure Letter para 2 confirms no final consent and no evidence of satisfaction of cl 11.3 conditions is in the data room.
- **Buyer wants:** Condition precedent requiring (a) effective, unconditional (or conditions-satisfied) consent under DD-002 cl 11.2, and (b) documentary evidence that the cl 11.3 conditions are satisfied, both before Completion; buyer-side approval of consent form.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; redraft as a hard CP with evidence of condition satisfaction.** Bluefen is ~30% of FY26 revenue (~AUD 3.6m) and a consent that is "delivered" but conditional or ineffective gives us no protection; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer.

## SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller position:** Cl 2/7 – ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding; release "to be provided following Completion". Disclosure Letter para 3 confirms not repaid, no discharge in data room.
- **Buyer wants:** Current payout letter from Riverlark before Completion; repayment directly from Completion funds via the funds flow; executed security releases/discharges (incl. PPSR) delivered at Completion.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject post-completion release; require payout-and-release at Completion.** On a debt-free/cash-free deal, completing with AUD 3.2m of secured debt and only a promise of later release is unacceptable; any post-completion release would require an irrevocable bank undertaking plus Amelia Frost approval, neither of which exists.

## SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller position:** Funds flow – DD-005 Completion bonuses (AUD 420,000) are "a matter for the Seller" and not itemised. Disclosure Letter para 5 confirms omission and is silent on payroll tax/superannuation/on-costs.
- **Buyer wants:** AUD 420,000 plus triggered on-costs (super, payroll tax, leave accruals as applicable) as a specific funds-flow line item funded by the Seller, or treated as Debt/transaction cost deducted from price, with the Seller confirming the on-cost position.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; require express line item or seller funding, plus on-cost confirmation.** "A matter for the Seller" with no mechanism means the Company (i.e. the Buyer post-Completion) will bear the cash cost, which silently shifts ≥AUD 420,000 of price.

## SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller position:** Cl 11.1 – indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; "considered adequate". Disclosure Letter para 4: DD-004 cl 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment; DD-010 shows AUD 180,000 open but is not bank-verified; no receipt or confirmatory assignment in data room.
- **Buyer wants:** Broadened indemnity covering non-transfer/defective title to SOW3 Project Materials, third-party claims, and costs of cure (including the AUD 180,000 or actual amount outstanding); preserve the cure route (pay outstanding SOW3 fees + obtain confirmatory assignment pre-Completion); request bank evidence of payment status either way.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject "adequate"; broaden the indemnity and require a pre-Completion cure or verified payment evidence.** The AUD 180,000 figure is unverified in both directions, so we need the indemnity to attach to the consequence (IP not transferring), not just the payment.

## SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident
- **Seller position:** Cl 4.6/Sch 6 – "preliminary operational matter", not expected to be material. Disclosure Letter para 6: ~1,240 records sent to an unintended external address; access, scope and notification duty undetermined; no confirmed breach, no loss amount.
- **Buyer wants:** Pre-Completion covenants to preserve logs, complete the investigation, provide written updates; a specific indemnity for losses, regulator action and notification costs arising from the DD-006 incident, outside the general basket/de minimis; no materiality concession either way.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the "not material" characterisation; add investigation covenants and a specific indemnity.** We assume no confirmed breach, harm or notification duty and make no numeric demand, but the Seller's label of "preliminary" is an assertion, not a verified update, and the exposure sits with us after Completion.

## SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller position:** Three renewals of AUD 110,000 (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs. Disclosure Letter para 8 does not state whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary-course.
- **Buyer wants:** Information request – timing, termination rights, whether accrued pre-Completion, whether renewals are committed or discretionary; then assess treatment.
- **Recommendation:** **Do not accept "ordinary course" as a conclusion; seek facts before taking a position.** Playbook does not require automatic Debt classification or price deduction, but the Seller's own disclosure admits it has not established ordinary-course status.

## SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller position:** Cl 12.3/13 default that limitations apply to "all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise"; cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 applying to "all Claims of any nature"; Tax/IP "settled under the general regime".
- **Buyer wants:** Title/Fundamental, Tax, IP, payment/price-adjustment and covenant claims each in their own clearly delineated regime; no general-regime default capturing them.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject; redraft so the general regime applies only to General Warranty Claims expressly listed, and each other category has its own cap/period.** Three separate drafting devices in the Seller draft operate as a hidden override that would swallow our Fundamental, Tax and IP positions.

## SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller position:** Title evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012. Disclosure Letter para 10 acknowledges this is simply the source relied upon and that the Buyer has not completed its own verification.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent evidence – ASIC company extract and historical searches, PPSR searches against Seller and Company, original share certificates, board minutes/authorities, Seller constitutional authority, and encumbrance confirmations (including Riverlark security over shares).
- **Recommendation:** **Do not accept DD-012 as proof; run independent title/encumbrance/authority verification and make Seller title warranties Fundamental (per SPA-N-004).** An internal register supplied by the Seller is not independent evidence and the Seller's own letter concedes as much.

## SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller position:** Tax and IP warranty positions "settled under the general regime".
- **Buyer wants:** Tax and IP remain OPEN; separate warranty/indemnity schedules to be negotiated with their own cap and time limits (tax typically aligned to statutory review periods); no unlimited liability assumed, no resolution assumed.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject "settled"; record Tax and IP as open items and reserve position.** Nothing in our authority process has agreed these terms and the Seller's statement is an assertion, not an agreed position.

---

## Suggested priority for the mark-up cover note
1. **Deal-blockers (must fix before signing):** SPA-N-004 (Title regime), SPA-N-005 (fraud carve-out), SPA-N-008 (Bluefen CP), SPA-N-009 (Riverlark at Completion), SPA-N-014 (category separation).
2. **Economic terms:** SPA-N-001, -002, -003 (cap/thresholds/period), SPA-N-010 (bonuses).
3. **Risk allocation / information:** SPA-N-006, -007 (disclosure/knowledge), SPA-N-011, -012 (Ironquay, DD-006), SPA-N-015 (title DD).
4. **Open / assess:** SPA-N-013 (Sandbar), SPA-N-016 (Tax/IP).

**Actions for the deal team:** (a) confirm with Amelia Frost that no fallback authority has been issued for cap or claims period on this draft; (b) issue a supplementary DD request covering Bluefen consent conditions, Riverlark payout, Ironquay payment evidence, bonus on-costs, DD-006 investigation status, Sandbar terms and independent title searches.

- **Recommendation:** **Reject "adequate"; broaden the indemnity and require a pre-Completion cure or verified payment evidence.** The AUD 180,000 figure is unverified in both directions, so we need the indemnity to attach to the consequence (IP not transferring), not just the payment.

## SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident
- **Seller position:** Cl 4.6/Sch 6 – "preliminary operational matter", not expected to be material. Disclosure Letter para 6: ~1,240 records sent to an unintended external address; access, scope and notification duty undetermined; no confirmed breach, no loss amount.
- **Buyer wants:** Pre-Completion covenants to preserve logs, complete the investigation, provide written updates; a specific indemnity for losses, regulator action and notification costs arising from the DD-006 incident, outside the general basket/de minimis; no materiality concession either way.
- **Recommendation:** **Reject the "not material" characterisation; add investigation covenants and a specific indemnity.** We assume no confirmed breach, harm or notification duty and make no numeric demand, but the Seller's label of "preliminary" is an assertion, not a verified update, and the exposure sits with us after Completion.

## SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals
- **Seller position:** Three renewals of AUD 110,000 (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs. Disclosure Letter para 8 does not state whether unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary-course.

## SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller position:** Cl 12.3/13 default that limitations apply to "all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise"; cl 9.3/12.8/20.5 applying to "all Claims of any nature"; Tax/IP "settled under the general regime".

## SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller position:** Title evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012. Disclosure Letter para 10 acknowledges this is simply the source relied upon and that the Buyer has not completed its own verification.
- **Buyer wants:** Independent evidence – ASIC company extract and historical searches, PPSR searches against Seller and Company, original share certificates, board minutes/authorities, Seller constitutional authority, and encumbrance confirmations (including Riverlark security over shares).
- **Recommendation:** **Do not accept DD-012 as proof; run independent title/encumbrance/authority verification and make Seller title warranties Fundamental (per SPA-N-004).** An internal register supplied by the Seller is not independent evidence and the Seller's own letter concedes as much.

## SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller position:** Tax and IP warranty positions "settled under the general regime".
- **Buyer wants:** Tax and IP remain OPEN; separate warranty/indemnity schedules to be negotiated with their own cap and time limits (tax typically aligned to statutory review periods); no unlimited liability assumed, no resolution assumed.
